title: Fighter jet scrambled and possibly fired on the 1952 DC lights
summary: Lou Elizondo tells of Fighter jet scrambled and possibly fired on the 1952 DC lights, about 1952 at Washington, D.C., and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: of discussion that actually there were some I think it was an f105 U fighter jet that was actually scrambled to intercept those lights those luminous objects and there's even one report reported account where perhaps uh they were asked to fire upon and may have actually hit one of them

plain: Lou Elizondo, who once led a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, talks on Jesse Michels' podcast about the glowing lights seen over Washington, D.C. in 1952. He says there was talk that a fighter jet, he thinks an F-105, was sent up to intercept them, and that one account says the pilot may have been told to fire and may even have hit one. If true, it would mean the US military shot at an unknown object over its own capital.
